Q0328

“There is nothing so beautiful and legitimate as to play the man…” — Michel de Montaigne (Essays III.13)

Verified English quotation. Primary source: Essays III.13. Theme: humanity.

Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Essays III.13 and files it under Renaissance Humanism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Michel de Montaigne

Michel de Montaigne (1533–1592) invented the modern essay as a form of self-study, combining classical learning with skeptical inquiry into custom and certainty.

How to read this passage

Philosophers ask what makes humans distinctive, what we owe one another as humans, and how “humanity” can include or exclude. This passage enters that discussion through humanity, order.

Concepts in this quote

Humanity
Humanity names both the species and the moral quality of being humane—bridging anthropology and ethics.
Order
Order names cosmos, ritual, law, and the patterned stability that makes shared life possible—or oppressive.
